name: cortex
description: A local, private coding agent for VS Code — like Cline, but powered entirely by your own Ollama models. No API keys, no cloud.

cortex.host.description: Base URL of your local (or remote) Ollama server.

cortex.model.description: Ollama model to use for the agent — must exactly match a locally pulled model name/tag (see `ollama list`).

cortex.autoApprove.description: Automatically approve file writes/edits and shell commands without asking for confirmation. Use with caution. Equivalent to approvalPolicy "full-auto".

cortex.approvalPolicy.description: Matches current Codex CLI. "untrusted": confirm every mutating tool (safest). "on-request": auto-approve mutations that are contained by the active sandbox (see cortex.sandboxMode) — anything the sandbox can't constrain still asks. "never": nothing asks for confirmation. Legacy values "suggest"/"auto-edit"/"full-auto" (this project's original naming) are still accepted.

cortex.sandboxMode.description: Matches current Codex CLI. "read-only": no file edits or shell commands allowed at all, regardless of approval. "workspace-write": file edits stay in the workspace and shell commands run inside a bubblewrap sandbox (Linux, requires bwrap) with network off by default. "danger-full-access": no containment — falls back to unsandboxed execution.

cortex.fastModel.description: Optional smaller/faster model used for read-only investigation steps (read_file, list_dir, search_code) — the main model is used once the agent needs to write code or run commands. Leave empty to always use the main model.

cortex.escalateModel.description: Optional stronger model (e.g. a cloud model like minimax-m3:cloud) to switch to after 2 consecutive tool failures/syntax errors in a turn — lets a small default model "call for help" instead of repeating the same mistake. Leave empty to disable.

cortex.testCommand.description: Command to run automatically once per turn after the agent edits files (e.g. "npm test"). If it fails, the failure is fed back to the model for one fix attempt before the turn ends. Leave empty to disable.

cortex.approveForMe.description: Codex-CLI-style auto-review: before falling back to asking you, a model call (cortex.fastModel if set, else cortex.model) classifies whether a pending action looks safe and auto-approves it if so. Anything it can't confidently call safe still asks you.

cortex.sandboxAllowNetwork.description: Allow network access from inside the command sandbox (only relevant when cortex.sandboxMode is "workspace-write").

cortex.sandboxCommands.description: Deprecated — use cortex.sandboxMode: "workspace-write" instead. Kept only so existing settings.json files with this key keep working.

cortex.autoApproveCommands.description: Command prefixes (e.g. "npm test", "git status") that run_command may execute without confirmation, even when cortex.autoApprove is off. A command is allowed if it starts with one of these prefixes.

cortex.provider.description: Which backend to send chat requests to. "openai-compatible" works with OpenAI itself, OpenRouter, LM Studio, vLLM, or any server exposing /v1/chat/completions.

cortex.apiKey.description: API key sent as a Bearer token when cortex.provider is "openai-compatible". Not used for Ollama.

cortex.webhookUrl.description: Slack or Discord incoming-webhook URL the agent's notify_webhook tool can post short status updates to.

cortex.mcpServers.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to connect to at startup. Each server's tools are added to the agent's toolset, prefixed "mcp_<name>_". Give either "command" (local, stdio) or "url" (remote, streamable HTTP) per entry.

headers.description: Extra headers (e.g. Authorization) sent with each request to a url server.

cortex.schedules.description: Cron-based recurring agent runs (e.g. daily TODO summaries, dependency checks). Runs unattended in read-only Plan Mode unless autoApprove is set on the schedule.

cortex.profiles.description: Named presets you can switch between with the "Cortex: Select Profile" command (Codex-CLI-style --profile). Each key is a profile name; its value is a partial override of host/provider/apiKey/model/fastModel/temperature/maxSteps/contextBudgetTokens/approvalPolicy/sandboxMode/sandboxAllowNetwork/approveForMe/autoApprove — anything you omit falls back to your base settings. Example: {"fast": {"model": "llama3.2:1b", "approvalPolicy": "on-request", "sandboxMode": "workspace-write"}, "careful": {"approvalPolicy": "untrusted", "sandboxMode": "read-only"}}.

cortex.activeProfile.description: Default profile (a key from cortex.profiles) applied on startup. The "Cortex: Select Profile" command overrides this per-session without changing this setting.

cortex.temperature.description: Sampling temperature passed to the model.

cortex.maxSteps.description: Maximum number of tool-call steps the agent may take per request before stopping.

cortex.contextBudgetTokens.description: Rough token budget for conversation history sent to the model each turn (chars/4 heuristic, no tokenizer dependency). Lower this for small-context-window models; when exceeded, the oldest messages are dropped and the model is told so explicitly rather than silently losing context.

cortex.useTerminal.description: Run shell commands in VS Code's visible integrated terminal (so you can watch them) instead of a hidden child process. Requires shell integration; falls back automatically when unavailable, and is bypassed for sandboxed commands.

walkthroughs.title: Set up Cortex
walkthroughs.description: A coding agent that runs on your own machine and uses your editor's language server.

steps.title: Install and start Ollama
steps.description:
Cortex talks to Ollama on your own machine. Install it from https://ollama.com, then run `ollama serve`.
[Check connection](command:cortex.setup)

steps.title: Pull a coding model
steps.description:
Run `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b` in a terminal, then pick it here.
[Select Model](command:cortex.selectModel)

steps.title: Choose how much to approve
steps.description:
Cortex asks before changing files by default. Destructive commands always ask, whatever you pick.
[Run Setup](command:cortex.setup)

steps.title: Try it
steps.description:
Open the Cortex panel and ask it to `list the files here`.
[Open Cortex](command:cortex.openChat)
